question:
Turn the SidekickMenu search box from on-by-default to opt-in: a consumer who renders <SidekickMenu items={items} /> sees no search input, and search appears only when the consumer passes searchEnabled={true}. Existing installations get the hidden default just by upgrading, because the default is resolved in code, not stored anywhere. Enabling search keeps every 1.7.0 search behaviour; no new prop is added. Because the default changes, the release must be a major version with a migration note and the reference docs updated.

What will be built:

1. R1: With no searchEnabled prop, <SidekickMenu items={items} /> renders no search input; the search box exists only when the consumer passes searchEnabled={true}.

2. R2: Passing searchEnabled={true} gives the consumer the full 1.7.0 search experience: the box shows, typing filters, clearing restores the previous section, search…

3. R3: The changed default ships as a major version 2.0.0 with an entry in docs/breaking-changes.md that names searchEnabled, states the new default and shows searchE…

4. R4: Every doc page that presents search as on by default is updated to present it as opt-in: README.md, docs/features.md, docs/examples.md, docs/api.md and docs/co…

5. R5: Tests prove the new default and keep proving the old search behaviour: a test asserts no input is rendered when the prop is omitted, and every existing search…

Assumed for you (tell me if any is wrong):

1. Search stays controlled only by the existing per-instance searchEnabled prop: no global config-provider switch, no runtime button and no keyboard shortcut to r…
2. When search is off, any active search term is dropped so the menu is never left filtered by a term the user can no longer see, and no empty-results state is sh…
3. Enabling search keeps 1.7.0's look and behaviour exactly: default placeholder 'Search menu...', autofocus default true, custom icon, filtering, and numbered sh…

Not included:

• A visible toggle, button or '/' shortcut that reveals search at runtime; only the prop turns it on.
• A global searchEnabled option on ZestSidekickConfigProvider.
• Changing search matching (searchTerms, label matching) or result ordering.
• Storing a per-user or per-app preference for search in localStorage or sessionStorage.

Are these right? Approve them, or tell me in your own words what to change.
optionLabel: Looks right, start designing, and write the documentation

question: Route after a disagreement: REV-1
answer: PERF-001 only requires that the built bundle not grow: I rebuilt the current tree in a scratch copy with the project's own rollup config and measured dist/index.js 122639 and dist/index.esm.js 122171 bytes, both below v1.7.0's 122706/122244, and the PERF-001 test at SidekickMenu.test.tsx:911 already enforces exactly that ceiling. The finding's premise is stale: SidekickMenu.tsx:42 is `const h = React.createElement;` and no MenuButton helper exists (bundle risk also removed), so both its size claim and its 'unproven' claim are contradicted by the code and the measurement. (route: challenge)
